title: Obtaining full contact for measuring polydimethylsiloxane mechanical properties with flat punch nanoindentation
author: De Paoli, Volinsky

steps.title: Initialize instrument and software
steps.instruction: Power on the Hysitron TriboIndenter (USA) equipped with the 1 mm diameter flat cylindrical punch tip and launch the TriboScan software.

steps.title: Calibrate transducer with air indentation
steps.instruction: Perform the standard air‑indentation calibration to set the transducer electrostatic force, verify the capacitor‑plate spacing, and confirm the 600 μN peak load, 10 s loading and unloading times, and the ~4–5 μm tip travel range in air; this also checks that the transducer maximum travel (~5 μm) will not be exceeded.

steps.title: Mount PDMS sample on stage
steps.instruction: Secure the PDMS sample (e.g., PDMS 10:1, 30:1, or 50:1) on the sample stage using the standard suggested procedure [4]; sample thickness may be 5 mm or 10 mm.

steps.title: Position tip and make first contact
steps.instruction: Manually move the stage so the flat punch tip is above the sample surface, then lower the tip in the Z‑direction until the first mechanical contact is detected; if the safety load is triggered, press the “AUTO ZERO” button on the transducer controller to reset.

steps.title: Advance stage to achieve full contact
steps.instruction: Increase the relative indentation depth by moving the sample stage upward in 1–2 μm increments (or larger if needed) while monitoring the loading stiffness; continue increments until the measured stiffness no longer increases with further depth.

substeps.instruction: Operate the indenter in open‑loop (pseudo‑load) mode.
Start with a 1–2 μm stage raise; record the loading slope.
Repeat the raise‑and‑measure cycle; keep total stage movement below 40–50 μm (up to 80 μm for very soft PDMS) to stay within the transducer capacitor spacing of ~80–100 μm.
Continue until the loading slope stabilizes; in the reported experiment this required 24 increments, reaching a total stage advance of ~48 μm.

steps.title: Confirm full contact stability
steps.instruction: After reaching the apparent plateau (e.g., at 48 μm stage advance), move the stage further to 50–52 μm and verify that the loading stiffness remains unchanged; then retract the stage by 2 μm and confirm the stiffness is still identical, demonstrating elastic, full‑contact conditions.

steps.title: Calculate reduced elastic modulus
steps.instruction: Determine the loading stiffness S from the plateau slope, then compute the reduced elastic modulus using Er = S / D, where D is the 1 mm flat punch tip diameter; for the PDMS 10:1 sample Er was found to be 3.8 MPa.

steps.title: Derive elastic modulus of PDMS
steps.instruction: Obtain the true elastic modulus by multiplying the reduced modulus by 0.75 (since E = 0.75 Er); for the PDMS 10:1 sample this gives E ≈ 2.85 MPa.

steps.title: Use fast loading to minimize viscoelastic effects
steps.instruction: Perform the indentation with a loading time of 10 s (or shorter) to reduce viscoelastic deformation during loading, as the slope of the fast loading curve is used for modulus calculation.
